title: 2026 elections: Early voting surges as first-time voters cast ballots in Chicago, Cook County ahead of midterms - ABC7 Chicago

 Early voting surges as first-time voters cast ballots in Chicago, Cook County 
 Early voting is surging as first-time voters are casting their ballots in Chicago and Cook County ahead of the midterm elections on November 3. By Leah Hope , Craig Wall Wednesday, October 28, 2026 10:39PM Share Follow ABC7 on Google CHICAGO (WLS) -- With the election now less than a week away, early voting numbers in Chicago and Cook County are running ahead of the pace set during the 2022 midterm election, a trend election officials and voter engagement advocates say reflects strong voter interest.
 On Wednesday, busloads of high school students traveled to the Chicago Board of Elections Supersite to cast ballots, putting classroom lessons about democracy into practice and, for many, voting for the first time.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 Among them was Butler College Prep senior Camren Redd, who said participating in the election was meaningful.
 "It feels great, great to participate in this," Redd said.
 Early voting in Chicago is up more than 11% compared with the 2022 midterms according to the Chicago Board of Elections. In suburban Cook County, election officials say turnout is increasing at an even faster rate.
 RELATED | 2026 midterm elections: Voter information in Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin 
 "We're on track to be 30% ahead of the 2022 gubernatorial election for suburban Cook County, and this has been because our students, our young people, have been civically engaged," Cook County Clerk Monica Gordon said.
 Mayor Brandon Johnson joined students from DRW College Prep on a bus ride to the polls as part of the Chicago Votes project, which promotes civic participation among young people.
 First-time student voters are casting their ballots early in Chicago ahead of the midterm elections on November 3.

 "I'm not mayor of Chicago without young people actively engaged in the process, 27,000 new voters voted in April of 2023. They did not vote in February of 2023, which was essentially the margin of victory," Johnson said.
 For some students, casting a first ballot brought a mix of excitement and uncertainty.
 "I did study pre-handed of who I should vote for and who is practically the right candidate, and I hope I made the right decision," said Elijah Candelaria, a senior at Pritzker College Prep.
 RELATED | Illinois Early Voting Ballot Tracker: See how many ballots have been submitted in each county so far 
 Other voters said they were encouraged by seeing young people participate in the election process.
 "I'm so really energized and excited to see the youth participating because this is everything that's happening now is going to really impact them in the future. So it's important that they voice their opinion and get involved in a process that's really going to impact them later," said early voter Britt Allen.
 Meanwhile, in Melrose Park, a coalition of immigrant rights organizations involved in the Democracy Project prepared volunteers to canvass neighborhoods and encourage eligible voters who face language or other barriers to voting to cast ballots.
 "After all we've seen this past year, getting out the vote this cycle is more important than ever and this November we have an opportunity, especially at the local level, an opportunity for the values we believe in," said Lawrence Benito, executive director of the Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights.
 The League of Women Voters Chicago said higher early voting numbers are encouraging but cautioned against voter complacency.
 "We're really sort of seeing people energized again about what participation looks like, and it's not just during election time. It's also in between. It's really sort of holding your elected officials accountable, showing up to meetings, you know, making your voice heard," said Jane Ruby, president of the League of Women Voters Chicago.
 RELATED | Chicago mayoral candidates submit thousands of nominating petition signatures 
 The election is six days away. While turnout could play a significant role in closely contested races, including school board contests, observers say participation patterns in November could also offer insight into voter engagement ahead of the municipal election less than four months away.
